Other Bels who acquitted themselves most notably were Ivan Beaumont, 28th in 17m. 46s., and Colin Nazar, 41st in 19m. 37s. Two other Bels, who were on this occasion running for their school, Shene Grammar, were Steven Wilson, 24th in 17m. 19s., and Stephen Jay, 56th in 22m. 12s.
Ryan Cup went to Ivan Beaumont, who totalled 93½ points, to finish a mere ½ point ahead of Jose Talhades, and 1½ ahead of Colin Nazer.
Steven Wilson was 3rd in 15.39. and Howard Breslin 9th in 16.23. Ivan Beaumont clocked 17.20 and Steven Jay 18.37. All recorded quite remarkable times for ones so young.

If we were to give a medal for perseverance it would have to go to Ivan Beaumont. Never seeming to have the success we all feel he deserves he nevetheless always turns out regardless of the weather or conditions.

Ivan Beaumont (a Boy) and Steve Walters (a Youth) also fancied their chances and took on the Seniors, putting up a couple of quite respectable performances and neither of them a long way down on the senior standard.

"Right, who's next" - Some of the Belgrave lads stand prepared to take on all-comers. Left to right: Gary Budinger, S.Watts, Mark Shippen, Robert Bashford, Steve Walters, Gary Wallace, David Didino and Ivan Beaumont.
Counting the best five events by each lad, a very successful and keen competition was eventually won by Mark Shippen from Ivan Beaumont and James Mead.

Whilst Mark Shippen has been setting a worthy Club best in the Pole Vault, at a height which must be considered for Youth and Junior records as well, Ivan Beaumont has been pushing out the Triple Jump 'frontier'.

Ivan Beaumont put in some good jumping and his 11.15m in the Triple Jump beats the Club Senior Boys record set 13 years ago. Particularly outstanding was Ivan Beaumont who equalled the Club Senior Boys 100m record and then leapt 5.38 metres to add 5 centimetres to the long jump record that had stood since 1961.
Outstanding was the triple jumping of 14 year old Ivan Beaumont who gained 2nd in the senior competition with a distance that beat his own boys record.
The events pursued by the four from Belgrave were: Triple Jump - Ivan Beaumont, High Jump - David Didino, 800 metres - Richard Danpure, and myself - Javelin.

Youngsters David Bailey and Ivan Beaumont continued their sprinting rivalry and in spite of running in 'A' and 'B' strings both clocked almost identical times.

He also set a new Club record in the Long Jump - 5.42 metres - beating Ivan Beaumont's old distance of 5.38 metres. Javelin thrower Peter Crosbie, in his first year in the Junior age group, demolished the opposition with 52.04 metres to gain another title.
